subfigures.description: One pressure-volume frame shared by two solid curves; not two separate panels or coordinate systems.

pixelFacts.description: The vertical axis has one upward arrowhead and label p near its top. The horizontal axis has one rightward arrowhead and label V near its end. Both extend a short distance past their common crossing; a 0-shaped origin label is below/left of the crossing. No numbered scales or units are shown.

Two thick solid decreasing convex curves lie in the positive quadrant. Each starts near the upper-left area, away from both axes, and ends at the right with positive pressure. The upper/right curve is labelled t2 near its right end; the lower/left curve is labelled t1 near its right end. The curves do not cross. They have no marked points, process arrows, dashed continuations or projection guides.
The source prints the separate comparison t2 > t1 in the upper-right interior.

One small upward unlabelled stroke is visible on the horizontal axis between the origin and the curve endpoints. It has no associated number, variable or unit; preserve it as an uncalibrated visible stroke, not a reading or a specified state.

textSupportedInterpretation.idealConstruction: The approved bilingual text identifies isotherms as hyperbolas for a fixed amount of ideal gas. A modern p=K/V construction is justified by that text, not inferred from original pixel coordinates.
textSupportedInterpretation.sameTemperature: Each curve contains states at one temperature; changes along that curve can connect different thermodynamic states. No phase change or marked direction of process is depicted.
textSupportedInterpretation.differentTemperatures: The two curves describe the same fixed gas amount at different temperatures. Their pressure ordering is compared only at the same volume.
textSupportedInterpretation.absolutePressure: p is absolute pressure, measured from vacuum, in the approved lesson.
textSupportedInterpretation.realGasLimits: The ideal relationship is only an approximation for real gases within the approved lesson's limits; no experimental real-gas calibration is claimed.

uncertainties: The origin glyph is visually 0-shaped; render the conventional zero, not a new named point O.
The small axis stroke is unlabelled and its purpose is not stated. Assign no coordinate value, tick interval, numerical calibration or point identity to it.

Curve coordinates, endpoint values and temperature ratios cannot be inferred from this unscaled image. The rendered positive constants and sampling domain must be disclosed as modern layout choices only.
